sections.code:
# Project: [Name]

## Stack
- Language: TypeScript 5.x (strict mode)
- Framework: Next.js 14 (App Router)
- Database: PostgreSQL via Prisma ORM
- Testing: Jest + Testing Library

## Commands
npm run dev          # development server
npm test             # run all tests
npm run lint         # eslint check
npm run typecheck    # tsc --noEmit
npm run build        # production build

## Coding Style
- 2-space indentation, single quotes, semicolons
- Named exports only — no default exports
- TypeScript strict — no `any` allowed

## Architecture Rules
- All database queries go through `src/lib/db.ts`
- API routes: return `{ data: T }` or `{ error: string }`
- Validate all user input with zod before DB operations

## What NOT to Do
- Do not use `any` — use `unknown` and narrow
- Do not write `console.log` in production code
- Do not modify `prisma/migrations/` manually

## Packages to Prefer
- Dates: `dayjs` (not `date-fns`, not native `Date`)
- HTTP: native `fetch` (not `axios`)
- Validation: `zod`

items.title: Be specific about one-right-way rules
items.body: 'Use dayjs not date-fns' is more valuable than 'handle dates carefully'. Concrete rules prevent the most common regressions.

items.title: List what NOT to do
items.body: Codex has strong opinions. Knowing your forbidden patterns prevents regressions better than stating the preferred pattern alone.

items.title: Keep it under 300 lines
items.body: Codex reads the whole file before each task. Very long files dilute focus — prioritise the rules that catch the most errors.
